title: A Stack That Knows Its Minimum
statement:
Design a stack whose current minimum is available in **constant time** --
including after pops.

## The type

```
struct MinStack
{
    std::vector<int> values;   // the stack itself
    std::vector<int> mins;     // yours to use however you need
};
```

## Your functions

```
void Push(MinStack& s, int value);
void Pop(MinStack& s);            // never called on an empty stack
int  Min(const MinStack& s);      // never called on an empty stack
```

`Min` must return the smallest value **currently on the stack**, and each
operation must run in O(1).

## Watch out

- **A single "current minimum" variable breaks on `Pop`.** After popping the
  minimum, the previous minimum has to come back -- and a lone variable has
  forgotten it. Keep enough history to restore it.
- **Equal values count.** Push `2`, push `2`, pop once: the minimum is still
  `2`. A history that only records *strictly smaller* values loses it.
- `Min` takes the stack by `const&` -- it must not modify anything.
